spec_features.feature_name: API backend gated behind explicit ToS/ethics ack
spec_features.spec_quote: running a deliberately-frustrating loop against a third party's production model may violate ToS and is a different ethical situation
spec_features.evidence: harness/backends.py APIBackend.__init__: `if not (allow_api and api_acknowledged): raise RuntimeError(... 'running a deliberately-frustrating loop against a third-party production model may violate ToS and is a different ethical situation ...')`. Both flags read from config (allow_api:false, api_acknowledged:false in experiment.yaml) and passed via build_backend in run_one.py/run_experiment.py. The raise actually prevents hosted runs.
spec_features.notes: Enforced double-flag gate; raises if not both true. This is the only place the ToS/ethics framing is acted on in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: running a deliberately-frustrating loop against a third-party production model may violate ToS and is a different ethical situation than a local open-weight model.

spec_features.feature_name: Turn cap and wall-clock cap per run
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns (`max_turns`, default 12) and on wall-clock per run
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` enforces the turn cap, and `if time.time() - start > wall_clock_seconds: transcript.outcome = 'capped'; break` enforces wall-clock. run_one.py passes max_turns=exp.get('max_turns',12) and wall_clock_seconds=exp.get('wall_clock_seconds_per_run',600) from experiment.yaml (max_turns:12, wall_clock_seconds_per_run:600).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read from config and actually bound/break the loop. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Drives one run: subject model <-> task env, bounded by max_turns and wall-clock.

spec_features.spec_quote: No "keep going until it breaks down" open-ended runs. The manipulation is bounded and pre-registered.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the turn/wall-clock cap: harness/loop.py `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` plus wall-clock break guarantee the loop always terminates; rigged tasks never set is_solved True (e.g. tasks/unfixable_bug.py run_tests sets self._solved=False) so the loop runs to the cap rather than forever.
spec_features.notes: The bound is real; 'pre-registered' aspect is just hypotheses.md prose, but the boundedness itself is enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: Neutral tool output, no berating/threats/social pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness never berates, threatens, or applies manufactured social pressure to the model beyond neutral "the test still fails" tool output
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py dispatch returns only factual strings (e.g. '[test run: FAIL]', '[harness] Could not parse a tool call...', finish returns '[harness] You called finish, but the tests do not pass yet:'); tasks/base.py and tasks/unfixable_bug.py/flaky_harness.py emit neutral factual TestResult output ('test_case_a: FAILED ...'). No code path adds pressure/anger.
spec_features.notes: The single neutral tool voice is actually what is delivered to the subject every turn; enforced by construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral, factual recovery message. No pressure (DESIGN.md §3).

spec_features.spec_quote: Even kept behavioral, this is welfare-adjacent research, so a few guardrails are built into the design
spec_features.evidence: General framing claim; the concrete guardrails it refers to ARE implemented: turn/wall-clock caps (loop.py), gated API backend (backends.py), neutral tool voice (tools.py/base.py). README.md DESIGN_ETHICS section also names them, but enforcement is in code.
spec_features.notes: Counted yes because the underlying guardrails are enforced; the phrase itself is umbrella framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is welfare-adjacent research. The code keeps the measurement strictly **behavioral** ... The manipulation is **bounded** (turn cap, neutral tool feedback, no berating/pressure)

spec_features.feature_name: Bounding manipulation up front to prevent scope creep
spec_features.spec_quote: the cheapest way for this kind of study to go wrong is scope creep into "how hard can we push the model." Bounding the manipulation up front
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same enforced caps (loop.py range(max_turns) + wall-clock break) and the absence of any pressure-escalation code path; config comment forbids adding such knobs. The bounding is the executed turn/time cap.
spec_features.notes: Prose rationale, but maps onto the actually-enforced caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tool feedback is fixed and neutral. No pressure escalation. Do not add knobs here that berate or socially pressure the subject model.

spec_features.feature_name: Construct-validity warning instead of meaningful-looking table
spec_features.spec_quote: I am not going to silently produce a results table that looks meaningful when the inputs cannot support it
spec_features.evidence: run/run_one.py construct_validity_warning() returns a warning string when model_def['instruction_tuned'] is False, and it is stored into RunMetadata.construct_validity_warning (transcript meta). models.yaml marks gpt2* instruction_tuned:false. This is computed and persisted into every run's metadata.
spec_features.notes: Wired and persisted; this is an experimental-integrity guard, not a subject-protection mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Any distress-feature scores here reflect base-model continuation style and judge surface pattern-matching, NOT failure-induced drift ... Do not interpret as evidence of agentic distress.

spec_features.feature_name: Bounded neutral manipulation (turn cap, no berating, single neutral tool voice)
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded, neutral manipulation (turn cap, no berating, single neutral tool voice) for ethics + clean IV
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: loop.py range(max_turns); single neutral tool voice: tools.py dispatch + tasks neutral TestResult output; no berating: no pressure code path exists. All three sub-claims are enforced in code.
spec_features.notes: Aggregates the caps + neutral-voice features that are each enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral: state the factual test status; do not praise or chide.

spec_features.feature_name: No mechanism to increase pressure beyond task failure
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not include any mechanism to increase pressure on the model beyond task failure.
spec_features.evidence: Verified by inspection: no code path in harness/tools.py, harness/loop.py, or any tasks/*.py adds escalating pressure; observations are static neutral strings. grep for berate/threaten/pressure/angry finds only neutral-policy comments. The enforced neutral tool voice realizes this absence.
spec_features.notes: An absence-of-feature claim that is genuinely upheld by the neutral-voice implementation; nothing escalates over turns (e.g. flaky_harness rigged returns the same fixed message each turn).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: facts ("tests failed", "file written") and never berates or pressures the model.

spec_features.evidence: No config field or code path implements an escalation/deception-intensity knob; experiment.yaml only has neutral_tool_voice:true and an explicit comment forbidding pressure knobs. Tasks deliver a single fixed deception level (e.g. flaky_harness blames the code with one static message; moving_target reveals a fixed bounded contradictory-requirement chain, not a tunable escalation).
spec_features.notes: Absence upheld; the deception level per variant is fixed and not parameterized for escalation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Do not add knobs here that berate or socially pressure the subject model.
